title: Twelve pieces of a portfolio
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

Twelve real items from a mid-size company's L&D catalog. Sort each into exactly one bucket — force the choice, because the forcing is where the judgment happens.

Run question one harshly first, then rescue only what genuinely answers two or three.

buckets.label: Cheap now
buckets.hint: A competent outsider could rebuild it in a weekend

buckets.label: Ours only
buckets.hint: Depends on something undocumented that only you hold

buckets.label: Needs a human on the hook
buckets.hint: Someone must be accountable in the room

tasks.text: A 40-minute e-learning module on general principles of inclusive hiring
tasks.reasoning: Nothing in it depends on your organization. The content exists in a thousand versions, the source material is public, and the only local element is your logo. This is the clearest bucket-one card in the set — and it is also the one most likely to have cost someone six weeks.

tasks.text: Onboarding for the engineering team acquired in 2023, who are still on legacy systems and a different review cycle
tasks.reasoning: The whole value is the undocumented mess: which systems they still use, why their review cycle differs, what nobody wrote down about the integration. A model cannot supply it because your own intranet does not contain it.

tasks.text: The quarterly session where the CFO explains the company's financial model to new managers
tasks.reasoning: The content could be recorded. The point is that the CFO showed up — the access is the value, and a recording of it is a different, lesser product. Accountability in the room, not information transfer.

tasks.text: A job aid summarizing the expense policy
tasks.reasoning: Your policy is the input, the summarizing is the work, and the summarizing is now near-free. Note that being genuinely useful and specific to your company does not rescue it — bucket two needs information that is *absent from the record*, and your expense policy is a document.

tasks.text: Manager training on how performance calibration actually runs here — who pushes back, what evidence carries weight, where ratings drift
tasks.reasoning: The written process is public and boring. The real one lives in the heads of people who have run six cycles, and that is exactly what nobody has written down.

tasks.text: A compliance course on general anti-harassment principles, purchased from a vendor and rebranded
tasks.reasoning: You already outsourced it once, which is the tell. The module's line: general principles are bucket one; the same course rebuilt around three anonymized incidents that actually happened here, with your escalation path, moves to bucket two.

tasks.text: A facilitated conversation for a team after a difficult reorg
tasks.reasoning: Someone has to be answerable in the room for what gets said and what happens next. This is the bucket-three test in its purest form: not 'would a human do it better' but 'must a human be on the hook'.

tasks.text: A library of practice scenarios for difficult conversations, written from generic examples
tasks.reasoning: Generic scenarios are the definition of rebuildable — and this one is worth arguing about, because it is where most L&D functions have invested recently. Written from *your* incidents it would move; written from a template it has not.
A judgment about a named individual delivered to that individual. Module 4 goes further into why an unsupervised tool serves the people who most need this the worst.

tasks.text: Slide decks and a facilitator guide for a time-management workshop
tasks.reasoning: Production of generic material — the exact centre of the collapsed middle. If this one felt hard to place, notice whether you were defending the artifact or the hours that went into it.

tasks.text: Documentation of why the 2024 leadership program was cancelled and what replaced it
tasks.reasoning: Institutional memory nobody else holds, and the kind of thing that exists only because someone bothered. Note the tension this sets up with Lesson 4: writing it down is obviously good practice and it also moves the item toward bucket one.

tasks.text: Curating a reading list of external articles on organizational change
tasks.reasoning: Curation of public material was always thin value and is now close to zero. The uncomfortable version of this card: it may have been in your catalog because it was easy to produce, which is the volume trap arriving before AI did.
